role: supplied-candidate independent adversarial whole-package reviewer; not blind rediscovery
original_target: For every finite d-dimensional simplicial complex K that is doubly Cohen–Macaulay over a field k (d>=1), can the minimal d-cycle pieces in Nevo Theorem 7 (OWR2005)/Theorem 3.4 (arXiv v2) be chosen to be k-homology d-spheres, with successive intersections containing a d-face and the stated reorderability? A counterexample with no k-homology d-sphere subcomplex refutes even the weaker covering demand.

definitions.2-CM: CM over fixed field k and every vertex deletion CM of the same dimension
definitions.CM: all face links, including empty-face link, have vanishing reduced homology below their dimensions
definitions.homology_sphere: global and every face-link reduced homology equal sphere of corresponding dimension; Swartz 2006 Section 4 explicit Gorenstein* convention

falsification_plan: Verify the proposed object is a finite abstract pure simplicial complex, with actual quotient links and deletion links, rather than a multicomplex or only local quotient data.
Verify all hypotheses of the construction theorem from its primary Sections 2–4, including ring, local algebra, and two-sided neighbor action.
Derive spectral/deletion and cohomological implications independently; test harmonic normalization, inequality directions, connectivity, all Reisner cases and reduced degree -1.
Test the sphere exclusion for local homology spheres over arbitrary fields, without silently substituting a global sphere-homology condition.

After sealing own mathematical assessment, examine provenance, priority and historical-versus-operative scope, then reproduce complete arithmetic/packaging controls and render each operative PDF page.
